title: PERFORM: playing the sound
description: PERFORM in depth: the keys and touch, six controls named for what you hear, honest controls, the XY pad, offers, Wander and coming home, the dock and MIDI, and all of it at once.

lines.text: PERFORM is where you play the sound.
Its controls are named for what you hear, and nothing in it ever stops the music.
Two rows of your computer keyboard play the notes: A to L are the white keys, and W to P the black.
Z and X shift the octave. Hold Shift for an accent.
On the screen keys, strike lower down for a harder note.
A MIDI keyboard plays as well, with velocity and pitch bend.
Velocity can shape the timbre, too.
With the touch row set to Bright, soft notes come out darker, and hard ones brighter.
Six controls are named for what you hear: Bright, Snap, Motion, Body, Grit and Space.
Hold a chord and ride Bright up. It swells, and the note never breaks.
Underneath, the patch's own knobs move with it.
Long-press a control to hear what it does on this patch.
Every patch gets its own wiring.
When one loads, PERFORM nudges each knob and listens.
Then it wires every control to the few knobs that move the sound its way.
A preset comes wired already, so it plays at once while PERFORM checks it.
On Bell Jar, Bright folds the wave instead. The name stays, and the knobs change.
Some controls only turn one way.
On this pad, Space stops at the centre toward close. It only turns toward far, and the line under it says so.
An amber control with a dashed ring is one this patch can't honestly reach.
Turn it anyway, and it asks for a sound that can.
Grit springs back, and B starts growing a variant aimed at grit.
When it lands, B says how much grittier it got, or that it found no way there. Listen before you take it.
The XY pad puts two controls under one hand.
Choose them here. Pick an amber one, and the pad tells you it can't move this patch.
Hold a chord, and draw.
The dials follow the dot. Double-click the pad to centre it.
Press Offer, and a variant of what you're playing grows in slot B.
It follows your hands. Every note you play sounds in both.
Hold Peek to hear B on its own.
Or ride Blend across. B plays at matched loudness, so you judge the sound, not the level.
Now the pad reads Next. Press it, and that's a pass.
Take the next one, and it's your sound.
Once you've heard it, either answer teaches the model what you like.
Keep makes the sound you hear home.
Then turn up Wander, and the model plays the controls with you.
A little, and ideas appear in B.
Further, and the knobs drift toward your taste.
All the way up, and it roams.
Structure never changes on its own. A new module only arrives as an offer.
Touch anything, and it waits for you. Freeze holds it where it is.
And Back glides you home, to the sound you kept.
In the dock, Hold latches the notes you play.
Unison stacks all four voices on one note.
Glide slides a line from note to note, and chords stay clean.
The arpeggiator plays a held chord at the tempo you set.
Sync puts the patch's own step pattern on that tempo too, so Loom's filter falls into time.
When you like what you hear, REC keeps it as a WAV file.
Plug in a controller and turn its knobs. The first eight you turn claim the eight controls.
Learn moves any control to the next knob you touch.
Pressure pushes Bright, and the mod wheel drives Motion.
The sustain pedal holds what you let go of, and MIDI clock sets the tempo.
With two tabs open, MIDI plays the one you used last. The other stands aside, and says so.
Now, all of it at once.
An arpeggio at eighty-four, Wander turned up, and an offer growing in B.
When it sounds right, take it on the downbeat.
That's PERFORM: play it, turn it, and let it offer.
Next, open the sound itself in PATCH, and see what it's made of.
And the guide's page on PERFORM has every detail.
